steps.title: Produce the genuine Gibbs domains
steps.text: Internally widen the upper bound to max(alpha,beta) only when invoking the existing score-square producer. Its actual probability and gradient norm-square L1 give vector MemLp2 and Bochner L1. The source theorem has no alpha<=beta premise; the dimension-zero case is retained.

steps.title: Recover ordinary full-space weighted integrability
steps.text: The canonical curvature-to-strong-convexity and Gibbs integrability providers yield integrable exp(-U) against ordinary volume. The actual tilted-law equivalence converts gradient L1 into exp(-U) times gradient L1 against this same volume. Its directional inner product is integrable for every v.
steps.formula: w=e^{-U},\quad w\in L^1(dx),\quad w\nabla U\in L^1(dx),\quad w\langle\nabla U,v\rangle\in L^1(dx).

steps.title: Integrate the derivative against the constant function
steps.text: C2 gives the ordinary Frechet chain rule Dw[v]=-w inner(gradientU,v). Apply full-space directional integration by parts to w and the constant1. All three required integrable products have been derived; the constant derivative is zero. No pointwise boundary-value or cutoff condition is assumed.

steps.title: Normalize and reconstruct the zero vector mean
steps.text: The canonical tilt integral divides each directional cancellation by the produced finite positive partition. Inner-product/integral commutation and real Hilbert extensionality identify the vector mean as zero. All objects use the same actual Gibbs measure.

steps.title: Keep the exact unnormalized convolution
steps.text: Reuse the actual smoothing producer. With ZV the original partition and A the literal source convolution including the printed Gaussian prefactor, the normalized potential is Ueta=Veta+logZV. Both partitions are positive and the source Veta is C2. Differentiate the constant shift, rather than asserting equal potentials.
steps.formula: A(y)=(\sqrt{2\pi\eta})^{-d}\int e^{-V(x)-\|y-x\|^2/(2\eta)}dx,\quad V_\eta=-\log A,\quad U_\eta=V_\eta+\log Z_V.

steps.title: Reuse the true everywhere Gaussian-convolution derivative
steps.text: The canonical Gaussian-convolution theorem internally produces probability and position L2 for the actual unreflected posterior R_y, and the directional derivative of Ueta. This is an everywhere literal tilted law, so no arbitrary conditional version is used at a null y.

steps.title: Construct the actual posterior Gibbs potential
steps.text: For each y define Wy=V+norm(x-y)^2/(2eta). Its C2 chain rule gives Hessian bounds kappa^-1+eta^-1 and1+eta^-1, both derived from the unchanged source binders. Canonical consecutive tilts show R_y=volume.tilted(-Wy). Positive eta is the complete analytic range.

steps.title: Cancel the actual posterior gradient mean
steps.text: The new shared mean-zero producer gives E_R gradWy=0 and genuine vector L1. Position L2 gives L1 of the quadratic gradient, hence L1 of gradV. Integrate the actual chain identity and rearrange. No expected-gradient identity or IBP domain is a source input.

steps.title: Identify the true smoothed score
steps.text: Compare the Gaussian-convolution derivative with the posterior cancellation, and use the Riesz inner-product characterization of gradient. The exact constant shift has already been differentiated. The resulting mean is under the true RGO posterior; it is not the own mean of the separate Gaussian-gradient output law.

steps.title: Reuse the same produced proximal selector and standardized law
steps.text: The existing allpositive standardized RGO theorem produces a measurable p, its stationarity, the affine pushforward r_y and its actual normalized Gibbs identification, with gradient-rho L2. The same p occurs in rho, the affine map, and the evaluator. No Jacobian or probability identity is assumed.

steps.title: Integrate the exact standardized chain rule
steps.text: The internally derived Frechet/Riesz chain identity gives grad_rho(u)=sqrteta times (gradV(p+sqrteta*u)-gradVp). Actual gradient-rho L2 supplies all needed first moments. Push the affine observable through the same r=T#R, use the exact inverse map, and integrate constants/scalars. This proves both printed Ex9 identities while leaving all bias/transport/cost bounds separate.
steps.formula:
ablaho_y(u)=\sqrt\eta(
abla V(p_y+\sqrt\eta u)-
abla V(p_y)),\quad
abla V_\eta(y)=
abla V(p_y)+\eta^{-1/2}\mathbb E_{r_y}
ablaho_y(U).
